title: Reduction isomorphism of the explicit corrected polynomial quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $A$ an $R$-algebra, and $I\subset R$ an ideal. Fix natural numbers $n,m$, natural numbers $N_i$ for $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(m)$, polynomials $g_i\in A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and elements $\epsilon_{ij}\in I$ for $j\in\mathrm{Fin}(N_i)$. Let $D$ be the finite set of pairs $(i,j)$, with any ULift relabelling. Form the explicit quotient $Q=A[t,\delta_{ij}]/(g_i-\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}\delta_{ij})_i$, where coefficients from $R$ are mapped into $A$. Put $B=(A/IA)[t]/(\bar g_i)_i$, with coefficientwise reductions $\bar g_i$. Then there exists an $R/I$-algebra isomorphism $Q/IQ\cong B[\delta_{ij}]$. Neither ind smoothness nor any evaluation map into another algebra is assumed.

proof.text: The maps from A and the polynomial variables to B[delta] send each corrected relation modulo I to zero, since epsilon_ij lies in I and each reduced g_i vanishes in B. Descend successively through the corrected relation ideal and IQ to define the forward R/I-algebra map.

Send A/IA and the old variables to their classes in Q/IQ. Each reduced g_i vanishes there, because the corrected relation holds and epsilon_ij vanishes modulo I. Descend to B and extend by sending each delta variable to its correction-variable class. This defines the reverse R/I-algebra map.

The two composites fix every coefficient, every old variable, and every correction variable. Polynomial and quotient extensionality give the inverse identities. Check scalar compatibility on lifts from R. ULift is a bijective relabelling; empty lists, I=top, and zero rings require no exceptions.
